description.en: Survey the landmark CNN architectures — LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, and ResNet — and understand the innovations that made each a milestone.

story_variants.en:
## CNN Architectures: LeNet to ResNet

Over 30 years, CNN architectures evolved from simple 5-layer networks to 150+ layer behemoths. Each generation solved a key limitation of the previous one.

### LeNet-5 (1998, LeCun)

The first successful CNN for digit recognition:
- 2 conv layers + 2 pooling + 3 fully-connected
- 60,000 parameters
- Input: 32×32 grayscale

### AlexNet (2012, Krizhevsky)

Won ImageNet with 15.3% top-5 error (previous best: 26%):
- 5 conv + 3 FC layers
- 60 million parameters
- Introduced: ReLU, Dropout, GPU training, data augmentation

### VGG-16 (2014, Simonyan)

Simple recipe: only 3×3 conv filters, depth matters:
- 13 conv + 3 FC layers
- 138 million parameters
- Very deep but very regular — easy to understand

### ResNet (2015, He)

Introduced **residual connections** (skip connections):

```python
# Residual block pseudo-code
def residual_block(x):
    identity = x
    x = conv(x)
    x = batch_norm(x)
    x = relu(x)
    x = conv(x)
    x = batch_norm(x)
    return relu(x + identity)  # skip connection!
```

### Architecture Timeline

| Model | Year | Depth | Params | ImageNet Error |
|-------|------|-------|--------|----------------|
| LeNet-5 | 1998 | 5 | 60K | N/A |
| AlexNet | 2012 | 8 | 60M | 15.3% |
| VGG-16 | 2014 | 16 | 138M | 7.3% |
| ResNet-50 | 2015 | 50 | 25M | 5.25% |
| ResNet-152 | 2015 | 152 | 60M | 3.57% |

> **Key Concept:** ResNet's skip connections solve the **vanishing gradient** problem. Gradients can flow directly through the shortcut path, enabling training of networks 10× deeper than before.

explanation.en: Add skip connection then activate — gradients flow both paths!

animation_sequence.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# ResNet skip connection block
class ResBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, channels):
        super().__init__()
        self.block = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(channels),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(channels)
        )
    def forward(self, x):
        return torch.relu(self.block(x) + x)  # skip connection!

block = ResBlock(16)
x = torch.randn(1, 16, 8, 8)
out = block(x)
print(f'Input == Output shape: {x.shape == out.shape}')

executionSteps.explanation: Residual block: core building block of ResNet
Two conv layers with batch normalization
Add input directly to output — gradients flow through shortcut
Residual blocks preserve dimensions — can stack many deep

under_the_hood.summary: Each landmark CNN changed how layers are stacked: LeNet proved the conv-pool pattern, AlexNet scaled it with ReLU and GPUs, VGG showed that small 3x3 filters stacked deep work better, and ResNet's skip connections let gradients pass through 50 to 152 layers.

steps.title: LeNet-5: convolution, pooling, then dense
steps.body: LeNet-5 took a 32 x 32 grayscale digit through two convolution and subsampling stages and then fully connected layers, about 60,000 parameters in total. The pattern, local filters with shared weights followed by shrinking the map, is still the skeleton of most CNNs.

steps.title: AlexNet: scale it up
steps.body: AlexNet (2012) used 5 convolution and 3 dense layers with about 60 million parameters, ReLU activations that train faster than tanh, dropout against overfitting, data augmentation, and two GPUs. Its large first filters (11 x 11, stride 4) shrank the 224-pixel input quickly.

steps.title: VGG: small filters, more layers
steps.body: Two stacked 3 x 3 convolutions see a 5 x 5 region, and three see 7 x 7. With C channels in and out, three 3 x 3 layers use 27C² weights against 49C² for one 7 x 7, and add two extra ReLUs. VGG-16 applied this rule throughout: 13 conv and 3 dense layers, 138 million parameters, most of them in the dense layers.

steps.title: ResNet: learn the change, keep the input
steps.body: A residual block outputs relu(F(x) + x): the layers learn a correction F added to their unchanged input. The derivative of F(x) + x with respect to x is F'(x) + 1, so during backpropagation the gradient always has a direct '+1' path around each block. That is what made 50- and 152-layer networks trainable.

steps.title: Bottlenecks keep deep nets cheap
steps.body: ResNet-50 uses bottleneck blocks: a 1 x 1 conv shrinks 256 channels to 64, a 3 x 3 conv works at 64, and a 1 x 1 conv expands back to 256. That is 69,632 weights against 1,179,648 for two 3 x 3 convs at 256 channels, which is how ResNet-50 has about 25 million parameters, far fewer than VGG-16.

under_the_hood.takeaway: Architectures improved by making depth work: small filters for efficiency, ReLU and normalisation for trainability, and skip connections so gradients survive. Residual connections now appear in nearly every deep network, transformers included.
